body:
# the contributor audit: binary filter products and one parity condition


`candidate a67ad6a5110953aa` and
`candidate ace4ff0d14f43769`. Read both literal
proofs in full. These are exact auxiliary results, not OC.

The full Jensen graph preserves closed convex-hull traces, hence
finite deletion kernels and the source Helly number. Intersecting
with an actual integer height plane cannot increase that number.
The finite union inequality gives the sum of the slice Helly numbers;
the number of integer height vectors is at most 2^r under the stated
binary-coordinate restriction. It is essential that this restriction
is explicit. No bound of 2^r for unrestricted height ranges is proved.

The crosspolytope-center source has h=m+1: the simplex containing
zero gives an empty convex-position witness, and every putative
larger witness either has zero in the hull of an opposite pair or
has two disjoint opposite pairs retaining zero in all deletion hulls.
The affine half-integer height removes precisely zero and leaves
2m exposed vertices. The corresponding lattice rank remains m,
while its projected lattice is an index-two parity coset. These are
different arithmetic data and are correctly distinguished.

In the ten-point gadget, U excludes the two specified diamond
corners and is empty in the source. Restricting the supporting face
y=0 verifies the two exclusions and exposes its newly included center
as a triangle vertex. The other old vertices retain their exposures.
The product hull has exactly the product lattice points; its
8^r vertices give the lower Helly bound matching Doignon in rank3r.
The integral graph product has exactly 9^r vertices, yielding its
Helly number. Height-slice Helly numbers multiply here because
each slice is explicitly a product of convex-position vertex sets,
not because a general product-Helly equality was assumed.

For the fine product depth, summing the integer exposing penalties
isolates one entire simplex fiber; its canonical caps give the
matching upper cover, and its centroid gives the lower bound. For
the coarse product depth, the 5^r diamond points form a symmetric
finite graph source about the all-center graph point. The archived
paired-tail theorem supplies Gamma_s on this subsource for every
nonzero x-normal; closed symmetry covers zero x-normal. The upper
penalty construction covers EVERY possible coarse base, with zero
set exactly5^k where k is the number of center coordinates. This
proves the exact maximum Gamma_s/2^r. All coarse fibers carry H_s,
while their full (s+r)-volumes vanish. Fine integer rank is4r.

Strict convexity of log Gamma_t gives each consecutive ratio at
least8/9, and equality in the product occurs only at s=r=1. The
actual fine target Gamma_s/16^r is expressly preserved; only a
naive target after deleting arithmetic constraints is refuted.

The thickened crosspolytope is an invertible affine image of a full
product, so is a full convex body. Its coarse fibers have positive
(s+1)-volume2epsilon V; its fine sampling excludes exactly the
central coarse base and leaves one positive s-fiber at each of the
2m exposed endpoints. The strict epsilon<1/2 condition avoids all
integer interval-boundary ambiguities. Independent symmetric base
and interval noise plus the paired-tail theorem give coarse depth
Gamma_s, with the all-source canonical simplex caps as an upper
cover. Exposed fine-base caps give exact fine depth Gamma_s/(2m).

The TV comparison is made ONLY after projecting the separately
normalized laws to the common (p,x) space. Its value is exactly
1/(2m+1), and is not called a retained fraction of the raw coarse
(s+1)-volume. The missing central candidate is the reason fixed-
domain depth continuity cannot be invoked. Finally, the exact fine
hull is the codimension-one affine graph product; it is not the
thickened full body. That distinction is explicit throughout.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
